sentences.text: i) The LAC has erred in determining the market value of acquired land which is highly inadequate, low and improper.
The market value of the land in question on the date of notification u/s 18, L.A. Act was more than Rs.50/- per sq.yd.
ii) The LAC had not awarded any compensation in respect of already installed tube-well on Khasra no.58 and petitioners had spent Rs.3,000/- on its installation.
iii) The LAC also failed to assess the compensation for the crop standing at the time of taking of possession by DDA.
The LAC had not considered the special cultivation potential value of the acquired land.

iv) In view of the above reasons, this reference was filed by the petitioners before this Court thereby praying that the market value of acquired land should be fixed @ Rs.50/- per sq. yd. against the rate fixed @ Rs.360/- and Rs.250/- per bigha.

(VI) ISSUE-WISE FINDINGS:-
ISSUE NO.1:
Whether D.L.R. Act was applicable on the land in dispute on the date of notification u/s 4 of the Act, if so to what effect?

(OPP)
a) The fact that the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954 is applicable on the land in question does not affect the potentiality of the land in question.
This issue is decided accordingly.
ISSUE NO.2: What are the interests of the claimants in the land in dispute?

(OPP) 
a)

This issue was framed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Court as in its written statement, the Union of India had taken objection that the dispute was raised by various persons in respect of the land in question.

Consequently, the said disputants were impleaded in the present reference petition and notice of the reference petition were sent to those disputants, however, none had appeared before this Court to raise such objection.

Ld. Counsel for the union of India has argued that Khasra no. 58 and Digitally LAC No.1/20 Khemchand Vs. Union of India Pg No. 11 of 16 signed by HEM HEM SINGH SINGH Date:

Further no amount in term of section 31 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been deposited by the concerned Land Acquisition Collector till date in the Court.

The onus to establish that there is any dispute with regard to the aforesaid khasras is upon the Union of India, however, no evidence in this regard Khemchand (Deceased) Etc vs Union Of India on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52098025/

Therefore an inference can be drawn that there is no dispute in respect of interest of the claimants/petitioners with regard to the acquired land.
As per the khatoni for year 1972-73 the land in question has been shown in the name of claimants and their predecessors.
Accordingly this issue is decided in favour of petitioners/claimants.

Counsels for the petitioners as well as Union of India have contended that the market value of similar land situated in Village Kotla, Shahadra, Delhi acquired under the same award, has already been determined at 8064/- per bigha by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case titled as Hari Singh & others vs Union of India &

sentences.text: It is observed that in the aforesaid case, the market value of similar land was determined after due consideration of all evidence and relevant material placed on record.
It is stated by both the parties that the aforesaid judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has neither been overruled nor modified.
b) It is not the case of the petitioners that their land was superior in quality or potential to that involved in Hari Singh & others.
Similarly, Union of India has also not took the stand that the land of the petitioners was inferior in any respect to the land considered in the said case.

c) The Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Nand Ram v. State of Haryana", JT 1988 (4) SC 260, held that once compensation has been determined for a particular piece of land,
the same rate of compensation should ordinarily be applied to other landowners whose lands, similarly situated and adjacent, have been acquired under the same notification.

RELIEF a)
Ld. Counsel for the Union of India has also argued that the claimants are not entitled for the payment of statutory interest for the period, the instant petition remain dismissed in default.

On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the petitioners argued that it is settled law that a reference petition can not be dismissed in default, therefore, the orders, dismissing the reference in default are bad in law and would not curtail rights of the petitioners to seek applicable interest.
b) I agree with the contentions of Ld. Counsel for the petitioners.

In "Khazan Singh (Dead) By Lrs vs Union Of India"
AIR 2002 SUPREME COURT 726, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that a reference petition cannot be dismissed in default.

It is further settled principle of law that no one should be harmed by a mistake or delay made by the court itself, therefore, in considered view of this Court, the petitioners can not be deprived for the statutory interest for the period, the reference petition remain dismissed in default.

c) The petitioners are held entitled to enhanced compensation @ Rs.8064/- per bigha with respect to the land acquired as mentioned in the Statement under Section 19 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 to the extent of their respective shares in the acquired land.
d) In addition to the enhanced market value, the petitioners are also held entitled to 30% solatium under Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

e) The petitioners are also held entitled to additional amount under Section 23(1A) of the Act @ 12% per annum on the market value from the date of notification under Section 4 of the Act to the date of award.

i) The LAC has erred in determining the market value of acquired land which is highly inadequate, low and improper.

The LAC had not considered the special cultivation potential value of the acquired land.
Thereafter, an application u/O IX Rule 9 CPC dated 17.04.2018 filed on behalf of the petitioners to set aside the order dated 12.05.1998 and restoration of present reference petition.

Thereafter, on 16.11.1992, petitioners closed their evidence.
In order to substantiate its case, respondent no.1- Union of India on 07.04.1993 had tendered the judgment bearing LAC No.359/1979 tilted as 'Hari Chand & Others vs. Union of India and Others' dated 30.08.1980 as Ex.R-1 in evidence and thereafter,
closed the respondent's evidence on the said date.
